finding.title: Fix Makefile check 15/15 cross-feature-deep-import detector — awk comparison always matches a feature against itself
finding.rule: Rule 0 (deterministic checker) / Rule 2 (no cross-feature deep imports) / AG-11
finding.area: tooling (learning_tracker/Makefile `make audit` check 15/15) — found while triaging this batch's cross-feature imports against the Rule-2 baseline
finding.why: match($0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b) scans the WHOLE grep -n line ('path:line:content'), so it always matches the importing file's own features/<name>/ segment first — the identical substring match($1,...) already captured into a[1] — because the file path precedes the import statement in that line. a[1] and b[1] are therefore always equal and the WARN branch can never fire, for any input; verified empirically by piping a real progress-to-learning cross-feature import line through the exact awk one-liner, which prints nothing instead of the intended warning. The check is warn-only so this never flipped CI either way, but it means the tool meant to enumerate the Rule-2 backlog has never actually enumerated it: lib/features/progress alone has a dozen-plus real deep cross-feature imports (chart_data_service.dart -> features/learning/domain/entities/completion_tier_filter.dart; lifetime_knowledge_providers.dart -> features/content_browsing/..., features/dashboard/..., features/tracks/...) that should appear in the WARN list and never will. 'make audit ... PASSED — all 22 greps clean' and this audit's own baseline note that 'ALL current cross-feature deep-import edges are baselined' cannot be verified against reality for Rule 2 — the source list is empty by construction, not by absence of violations.
finding.recommendation: Fix the awk to compare the import target's feature against the importing file's own feature — e.g. restrict the second match() to substr($0, length($1)+1) so it only scans the import-statement portion of the line — then re-run make audit and reconcile the resulting edge count against the digest's baseline claim, which today only actually covers check 14.
acceptance_criteria: Feeding a synthetic cross-feature import line through check 15's grep+awk pipeline prints the WARN line; feeding a same-feature deep-import line does not.
make audit's check 15 output, run against current HEAD, lists a non-empty (or explicitly justified empty) set of real cross-feature deep-import edges.
